questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of discontinuous variation in humans?
questions.explanation: A person is A, B, AB or O with nothing in between, so blood group falls into clear-cut categories controlled by one gene and unaffected by the environment. Height, mass and skin colour are polygenic and environmentally influenced, giving a smooth range of values.

distractorRationale.a: Height varies smoothly and is affected by diet as well as by many genes
distractorRationale.b: Body mass is strongly influenced by diet and activity
distractorRationale.d: Skin colour is polygenic and grades continuously between extremes

questions.stem: The sex of a human child is determined by

options.text: the mother, because she carries the developing baby
the father, because only he produces both X-bearing and Y-bearing gametes
the diet of the mother during pregnancy
the number of chromosomes in the egg cell

questions.explanation: A mother is XX and every egg she produces carries an X. A father is XY and produces X and Y sperm in equal numbers, so whether the child is XX or XY depends entirely on which of his sperm reaches the egg first.

distractorRationale.a: Carrying the pregnancy has no bearing on which sperm fertilised the egg
distractorRationale.c: Diet cannot alter the sex chromosome already present in the zygote
distractorRationale.d: All normal eggs carry 23 chromosomes, one of which is always an X

questions.stem: Two parents both have the sickle cell trait (genotype AS). What is the probability that any one of their children will have sickle cell anaemia?
questions.explanation: The cross AS × AS gives offspring in the ratio 1 AA : 2 AS : 1 SS, so one quarter are expected to be SS and therefore to have sickle cell anaemia. Half will carry the trait like their parents and a quarter will be entirely normal.

distractorRationale.a: Both parents carry the S allele, so an SS child is possible
distractorRationale.c: 1 in 2 would be the proportion with the trait, AS, not with the disease
distractorRationale.d: 3 in 4 is the proportion who will not have the disease

questions.stem: A couple have had three daughters. What is the probability that their fourth child will be a son?

options.text: Certain, because they are due a son
1 in 2, because each fertilisation is an independent event
1 in 4, because they already have three girls
3 in 4, because the chance increases with each girl

questions.explanation: Whether an X-bearing or a Y-bearing sperm fertilises the egg is decided afresh at each conception, and the two kinds are produced in equal numbers. Previous pregnancies leave no trace on the process, so the probability remains one half every time.

distractorRationale.a: Biology keeps no record of past outcomes, so nothing is ever due
distractorRationale.c: This confuses the chance of four girls in a row with the chance for one particular child
distractorRationale.d: The probability does not accumulate across pregnancies

questions.stem: Colour blindness is much commoner in men than in women because the allele is

options.text: dominant and carried on the Y chromosome
recessive and carried on the X chromosome, and a man has only one X
found only in male body cells
caused by a shortage of vitamin A in men

questions.explanation: A woman has two X chromosomes, so a normal allele on one X masks a faulty allele on the other and she is only a carrier. A man has a single X and a Y that lacks the corresponding gene, so one faulty allele is enough to make him colour blind.

distractorRationale.a: The allele is recessive and lies on the X, not the Y
distractorRationale.c: Women carry the allele too, but usually without expressing it
distractorRationale.d: Colour blindness is inherited, unlike night blindness which is caused by vitamin A deficiency

questions.stem: A person of blood group AB has both A and B antigens on the surface of the red cells. This is because the alleles for A and B are

options.text: codominant, so both are fully expressed
incompletely dominant, giving an intermediate antigen

questions.explanation: Codominance means neither allele masks the other and both products appear, so a person with one allele for A and one for B makes both antigens. This differs from incomplete dominance, where the heterozygote shows a genuinely intermediate phenotype.

distractorRationale.b: Both are dominant to the O allele, so neither is recessive
distractorRationale.c: There is no blended intermediate antigen; both antigens are present separately
distractorRationale.d: The ABO gene lies on an autosome, not on a sex chromosome

questions.stem: Why has the sickle cell allele remained common in parts of West Africa despite the severity of sickle cell anaemia?

options.text: Because SS individuals are especially healthy
Because AS carriers have some resistance to malaria and so survive to reproduce
Because the allele arose only recently

questions.explanation: Heterozygotes are usually healthy and are less severely affected by malaria than AA individuals, so in malarial regions they have a survival advantage and pass the S allele on. Natural selection therefore keeps the allele at a substantial frequency even though SS individuals suffer greatly.

distractorRationale.a: SS individuals suffer painful crises, anaemia and a reduced life expectancy
distractorRationale.c: The allele behaves as recessive for the disease; only SS individuals are affected
distractorRationale.d: The allele is ancient, and recency would not explain a high frequency

questions.stem: Continuous variation such as height is influenced by both many genes and the environment.
questions.explanation: True. Height is polygenic, so many genes each make a small contribution and the combined effect produces a smooth range rather than distinct categories. Nutrition, illness in childhood and other environmental factors then modify the outcome, which is why identical twins raised differently can differ in height.

questions.stem: A poultry farmer keeps and breeds only from the hens that lay the most eggs, generation after generation. This practice is called
questions.explanation: The farmer, rather than the environment, decides which individuals reproduce, so the alleles for high egg production become progressively commoner in the flock. It depends entirely on the existence of inherited variation among the hens to select from.

distractorRationale.a: In natural selection the environment does the selecting, with no human choice involved
distractorRationale.c: Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction in plants
distractorRationale.d: Genetic counselling advises people about the risk of passing on a genetic disorder

questions.stem: Using a genetic cross, show why a man and a woman who both have the genotype AS have a one in four chance of producing a child with sickle cell anaemia. Explain why genotype testing before marriage is advised in Nigeria, and state the advantage the AS genotype confers.
markingGuide: Symbols defined: A is the allele for normal haemoglobin, S the allele for sickle haemoglobin (1 mark)
Parental genotypes stated as AS and AS, both with sickle cell trait (1 mark)
Gametes shown: each parent produces A and S gametes in equal numbers (2 marks)
Punnett square or cross correctly giving AA, AS, AS and SS (3 marks)
Ratio interpreted: 1 AA normal : 2 AS trait : 1 SS sickle cell anaemia, so a one in four risk at every pregnancy (2 marks)

Reason for testing: the couple can be informed of the recurring risk before starting a family and make decisions with full knowledge, since the risk applies afresh to each pregnancy rather than only once in four children (2 marks)
Advantage of AS: heterozygotes have increased resistance to malaria, which is why the allele has persisted in malarial regions (1 mark)
questions.explanation: The cross AS × AS yields 1 AA : 2 AS : 1 SS, so the one in four risk is a probability that applies independently to each pregnancy rather than a guarantee of one affected child in four. Testing matters because both carriers are healthy and would otherwise have no way of knowing the risk, and the persistence of the allele is explained by the malaria resistance of the AS genotype.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes continuous variation?

options.text: It shows a range of phenotypes.
It is only influenced by one gene.
It is not affected by environmental factors.

questions.explanation: Continuous variation refers to traits that can take on a range of values, such as height or weight, rather than fitting into distinct categories. These traits are typically influenced by multiple genes and environmental factors.

distractorRationale.a: This describes discontinuous variation.
distractorRationale.c: Continuous variation is influenced by multiple genes.
distractorRationale.d: Environmental factors play a significant role in continuous variation.

questions.stem: In humans, sex-linked traits are typically associated with which chromosome?
questions.explanation: Sex-linked traits are primarily associated with the X chromosome in humans. Males have one X and one Y chromosome, while females have two X chromosomes, making the inheritance of these traits different between genders.

distractorRationale.a: Autosomes do not carry sex-linked traits.
distractorRationale.b: The Y chromosome carries few genes and is not primarily responsible for sex-linked traits.
distractorRationale.d: The Z chromosome is not present in humans.

questions.stem: What is the expected phenotypic ratio of offspring from a cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa) for a trait?
questions.explanation: When two heterozygous parents (Aa) are crossed, the expected phenotypic ratio of their offspring is 3:1. This means that for every four offspring, three will display the dominant trait and one will display the recessive trait.

distractorRationale.a: A 1:1 ratio occurs in monohybrid crosses of heterozygous and homozygous parents.
distractorRationale.c: A 1:2:1 ratio indicates genotypic outcomes, not phenotypic.
distractorRationale.d: A 9:3:3:1 ratio is typical of a dihybrid cross.

questions.stem: Which of the following blood groups can a child with blood group O have as parents?
questions.explanation: A child with blood group O must inherit an O allele from both parents. Therefore, the only possible parental blood groups that can produce an O child are O and O, or a combination of A and B if they are both carriers of the O allele.

distractorRationale.a: A child with blood group O cannot be produced by parents with A and B blood groups unless they both carry the O allele.
distractorRationale.b: Two A parents could produce an O child only if both are carriers.
distractorRationale.c: Two B parents could produce an O child only if both are carriers.

questions.stem: Sickle cell disease is caused by a mutation in which gene?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease is caused by a mutation in the HBB gene, which encodes the beta-globin subunit of hemoglobin. This mutation leads to the production of abnormal hemoglobin known as hemoglobin S.

distractorRationale.b: The HBA gene encodes the alpha-globin subunit, not beta-globin.
distractorRationale.c: The HBC gene is related to another variant of hemoglobin, not sickle cell disease.
distractorRationale.d: The HBD gene is not associated with sickle cell disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about sex determination in humans is true?

options.text: The presence of a Y chromosome determines maleness.
Females can only pass on Y chromosomes.

questions.explanation: The presence of a Y chromosome in humans is what determines maleness. Males typically have one X and one Y chromosome, while females have two X chromosomes.

distractorRationale.a: Females have XX chromosomes, not XY.
distractorRationale.b: Males have one X and one Y chromosome, not two Xs.
distractorRationale.d: Females can only pass on X chromosomes.

questions.stem: What is the role of genetic counseling in sickle cell disease?

options.text: To provide information about inheritance patterns.
To promote the sickle cell trait.
To eliminate sickle cell alleles from the population.

questions.explanation: Genetic counseling for sickle cell disease provides individuals and families with information about the inheritance patterns of the disease, helping them understand the risks of having affected children. It does not cure the disease or promote the trait.

distractorRationale.a: Genetic counseling does not cure diseases; it provides information.
distractorRationale.c: The goal is to inform about risks, not promote the trait.
distractorRationale.d: Eliminating alleles is not the aim of genetic counseling.

questions.stem: What type of inheritance pattern does color blindness follow?
questions.explanation: Color blindness is primarily inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern, meaning that the gene responsible for the condition is located on the X chromosome. Males are more frequently affected due to having only one X chromosome.

distractorRationale.a: Autosomal dominant traits would appear in every generation.
distractorRationale.b: Autosomal recessive traits require two copies of the allele to be expressed.
distractorRationale.d: Y-linked traits are only passed from father to son.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of discontinuous variation?

options.text: It is influenced by multiple genes.
It is affected by environmental factors.

questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation results in distinct categories, such as blood type or the presence of a certain trait. Unlike continuous variation, it is not influenced by multiple genes or environmental factors.

distractorRationale.a: This describes continuous variation, not discontinuous.
distractorRationale.b: A bell-shaped curve is typical of continuous variation.
distractorRationale.d: Environmental factors influence continuous variation.

questions.stem: Which of the following genetic disorders is caused by a single gene mutation?
questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the CFTR gene, making it a single-gene disorder. In contrast, Down syndrome and the other syndromes listed are typically caused by chromosomal abnormalities.

distractorRationale.b: Down syndrome is caused by an extra chromosome (trisomy 21).
distractorRationale.c: Turner syndrome results from a missing X chromosome.
distractorRationale.d: Klinefelter syndrome is caused by an extra X chromosome in males.

questions.stem: The phenotypic expression of a trait influenced by multiple genes is known as?
questions.explanation: Polygenic inheritance refers to traits that are influenced by multiple genes, leading to a continuous range of phenotypes. Examples include height and skin color in humans.

distractorRationale.b: Monogenic inheritance involves a single gene affecting a trait.
distractorRationale.c: Epistasis refers to the interaction between genes, not the number of genes involved.
distractorRationale.d: Codominance describes a situation where both alleles are expressed equally.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a characteristic of continuous variation?

options.text: It is influenced by a few genes.
It exhibits a range of phenotypes.
It is only affected by environmental factors.

questions.explanation: Continuous variation refers to traits that can take on a range of values, such as height or weight. These traits are influenced by multiple genes and environmental factors, resulting in a spectrum of phenotypes.

distractorRationale.a: This option is incorrect because continuous variation is influenced by many genes, not just a few.
distractorRationale.b: This option describes discontinuous variation, which has distinct categories.
distractorRationale.d: While environmental factors do play a role, continuous variation is primarily influenced by multiple genes.

questions.stem: What is the expected genotype ratio of offspring from a cross between two homozygous parents (AA and aa)?
questions.explanation: When two homozygous parents are crossed (AA x aa), all offspring will inherit one allele from each parent, resulting in 100% AA genotype. This demonstrates the principle of dominance in genetics.

distractorRationale.a: This ratio applies to a cross between two heterozygous parents, not homozygous.
distractorRationale.b: This ratio is typical of a monohybrid cross between heterozygous parents.
distractorRationale.c: This ratio is seen in a cross between a homozygous and a heterozygous parent.

questions.stem: Which of the following blood group genotypes can produce a child with blood group A?
questions.explanation: A child with blood group A can inherit either the AA or AO genotype from their parents. The A allele is dominant over the O allele, allowing for the A phenotype to be expressed.

distractorRationale.b: BB and BO can produce a child with blood group B, not A.
distractorRationale.c: AB and OO can produce a child with blood group AB or O, not A.
distractorRationale.d: AA and BB will produce children with blood groups A and B, but not A alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about sex-linked inheritance is true?

options.text: It is passed on through the X chromosome.

questions.explanation: Sex-linked inheritance typically involves genes located on the X chromosome, which can affect both males and females. Males are more frequently affected by X-linked recessive disorders due to their single X chromosome.

distractorRationale.a: This option is incorrect as sex-linked traits can affect both sexes.
distractorRationale.c: Sex-linked traits can indeed be inherited, contrary to this statement.
distractorRationale.d: This option is misleading; while males are often more affected, females can also be carriers.

questions.stem: In humans, which of the following is an example of a sex-linked trait?
questions.explanation: Color blindness is a classic example of a sex-linked trait, as it is often associated with the X chromosome. Males are more frequently affected because they have only one X chromosome.

distractorRationale.a: Blood type is determined by multiple alleles and not linked to sex chromosomes.
distractorRationale.b: Sickle cell anemia is an autosomal recessive condition, not sex-linked.
distractorRationale.d: Height is influenced by multiple genes and is not a sex-linked trait.

options.text: A mutation in the hemoglobin gene

questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease is primarily caused by a mutation in the hemoglobin gene (HBB), leading to the production of abnormal hemoglobin that distorts red blood cells into a sickle shape.

distractorRationale.a: This option is incorrect as sickle cell disease is genetic, not caused by an infection.
distractorRationale.c: Vitamin C deficiency does not cause sickle cell disease.
distractorRationale.d: An autoimmune disorder is unrelated to the genetic mutation causing sickle cell disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following blood group combinations can result in a child with blood group AB?
questions.explanation: A child can inherit blood group AB from parents with genotypes AB and AB, or A and B blood types, where one parent contributes an A allele and the other a B allele.

distractorRationale.a: AA and AO can only produce A or O blood groups.
distractorRationale.c: A and B can produce AB, but not exclusively AB.
distractorRationale.d: O and O can only produce blood group O.

questions.stem: What is the expected phenotypic ratio of offspring from a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (AaBb x AaBb)?
questions.explanation: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (AaBb x AaBb), the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is 9:3:3:1, representing the combinations of two traits.

distractorRationale.a: This ratio applies to a monohybrid cross, not a dihybrid.
distractorRationale.c: This ratio is typical of a monohybrid cross between heterozygous parents.
distractorRationale.d: This ratio applies to a cross between two homozygous parents.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of genetic counseling?

options.text: To provide medical treatment for genetic disorders
To inform individuals about their genetic risks and options

questions.explanation: Genetic counseling is primarily aimed at informing individuals about their genetic risks, potential inherited conditions, and options for family planning or management.

distractorRationale.a: While genetic counselors may work with medical professionals, they do not provide treatment directly.
distractorRationale.c: Conducting genetic research is not the main focus of genetic counseling.
distractorRationale.d: Diagnosis is typically done by medical professionals; genetic counselors provide information and support.

distractorRationale.a: Height is an example of continuous variation.
distractorRationale.b: Eye color can also show continuous variation due to multiple genes.
distractorRationale.c: Skin color is influenced by multiple genes and shows continuous variation.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of using sickle cell trait carriers in breeding programs?

options.text: They produce offspring with sickle cell disease.
They can only produce normal hemoglobin.
They are unaffected by sickle cell disease.

questions.explanation: Sickle cell trait carriers (genotype AS) have a selective advantage in malaria-endemic areas as they exhibit some resistance to malaria while not suffering from the severe effects of sickle cell disease.

distractorRationale.a: This option is incorrect; carriers do not produce offspring with sickle cell disease unless both parents are carriers.
distractorRationale.c: Carriers produce both normal hemoglobin and sickle hemoglobin.
distractorRationale.d: While carriers do not have sickle cell disease, they can pass the trait to their offspring.
